title: Standardize agent research: auto-research.md, auto-research/ layout, and a mirror of research/
body:
## What this changes

This PR proposes a standard `auto-research/` folder that can be reused across auto-research repos, plus a root-level instruction file for agents. No mathematical claim or κ change.

1. **`auto-research.md` (root)**: the entry point for any agent starting a session. It links the community prompt by @Mister-Meeseeks (https://gist.github.com/Mister-Meeseeks/9f768c8b1a3e7d2e70b8e5c0bc18ab7e) as the authoritative version and summarises its six steps: orient, pick a track, claim scope, run one bounded experiment, verify and package, hand off. It also sets the package layout and ground rules: exact replays only, honest scope, credit predecessors, disclose models and harnesses, use your own compute.
2. **`auto-research/README.md`**: the package standard. One directory per submission, `auto-research/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<handle>-<slug>/`, containing `README.md`, `RESULT.json`, `verify.py`/`verify.sh`, `MANIFEST.json` and `NOTICE.md`, with a `RESULT.json` schema.
3. **A byte-identical mirror of `research/` under `auto-research/`**: all 209 entries (20,119 files). Git stores the copies as the same blobs, so the repository barely grows. The diff is large only because every path appears twice.

## What it deliberately does not change

`research/` itself is untouched; its tree hash `66af7031…` equals current `main`. More than 1,600 files (verifiers, manifests, hash pins and 52 Makefile lines) reference `research/...` paths, so moving the folder would break existing certificates. Existing verifiers keep running from `research/`. New packages go directly into `auto-research/`. Retiring the old path can be a separate, reviewed change once pins are updated.

## Checks

- `git rev-parse HEAD:research` equals `main`'s, so research/ is unchanged.
- `auto-research/` contains every tracked `research/` file, including force-tracked ones, plus `README.md`: 20,120 files.
- No verifier, certificate, Makefile or `upstream/` file is modified.
